oewn-02160589-s.learner: made for one person or thing, or typical of one person or thing.
examples: We booked a single room for one night.
The small cabin had only a single bed.

oewn-00541609-s.learner: aimed at only one thing or goal, and not split among several.
examples: Her single devotion to her children left her no time for anything else.

oewn-01973805-s.learner: applying in the same way to everyone or everything.
examples: The new law gave the whole country a single code for all its courts.

oewn-02228429-a.learner: of flowers, usually having only one ring of petals.
examples: She grew single roses, with just one ring of petals around the middle.

oewn-00818664-v.learner: to refuse to accept or believe something.
examples: He kept denying his illness until he could no longer walk.

oewn-00818828-v.learner: to refuse to recognize someone or something, or to refuse to openly accept them.
examples: When the soldiers asked, he denied his own brother.

oewn-02217856-v.learner: to stop yourself from having something, especially something you enjoy.
examples: She denied herself sweets for the whole winter.

oewn-01070402-v.learner: in a court case, to formally say that a fact stated by the other side is not true.
examples: In its answer to the lawsuit, the company formally denied the facts stated by the other side.

oewn-00380562-n.learner: an act that mixes things together in a disorderly way, so that they can no longer be told apart.
examples: The old story tells of the confusion of tongues at the Tower of Babel.

oewn-07232009-n.learner: the act of formally making a person known to another person or to the public.
examples: Miss Darcy and her brother appeared, and this formidable introduction took place.
Elizabeth had mentioned her name to her mother on her Ladyship's entrance, though no request of introduction had been made.

oewn-06408573-n.learner: the first part of a piece of writing, a speech, or another message.
examples: The introduction explains what the rest of the book is about.

oewn-00238889-n.learner: the act of beginning something new.
examples: The introduction of the new car drew large crowds to the show.

oewn-00241051-n.learner: the act of starting something for the first time, or of bringing in something new.
examples: The introduction of free schools changed life in the town.

oewn-07177626-n.learner: a new idea or plan that someone puts forward.
examples: The latest introduction from the council is a plan to close the park at night.

oewn-06426492-n.learner: a simple book or text that teaches the basic parts of a subject.
examples: She bought a short introduction to chemistry written for beginners.

oewn-00321678-n.learner: the act of putting one thing into another.
examples: The introduction of the needle into the vein must be done carefully.
By noon they had performed every task on the list.

oewn-01650408-v.learner: to cause something to appear or to happen.
examples: The heavy rain provoked a landslide on the hill.

oewn-06743312-n.learner: a statement that something is true.
examples: Nobody believed his claim that he had been at home all night.

connotation.why: set against 'statement', may leave the truth open to doubt

oewn-05188726-n.learner: a right to something that is settled or accepted by others.
examples: She has a strong legal claim to the house.

oewn-07206789-n.learner: a demand; something that is asked or required of someone.
examples: Society has claims on us all.
You refuse to obey the claims of duty, honour, and gratitude.

oewn-01993887-v.learner: to go down under the surface.
examples: The boat hit a rock and sank.

oewn-01989937-v.learner: to fall or go down to a lower place or level.
examples: He sank to his knees on the wet grass.

oewn-01975943-v.learner: to go down into something soft, or into a place as if it were soft.
examples: She sank into the deep armchair with a sigh.
My heart sank when I read the letter.
The sun sank slowly behind the hills.

oewn-01532886-v.learner: to push something deep into something else.
examples: The dog sank its teeth into the bone.

oewn-02743444-v.learner: to rightly be placed in a certain class or group of things.
examples: Spiders do not belong among the insects.
Among the rich guests, she felt that she did not belong.

oewn-02725805-v.learner: to be a part of something, or a thing added to it.
examples: The lid that belongs to this pot is missing.

oewn-14487589-n.learner: something wrong or imperfect in a part or system of the body.
examples: The baby was born with a heart defect.
